body: I am completely willing to debug and submit a PR if this is indeed a valid bug, I just need some guidance figuring out what code to look at. Webpack is a big project!

Thanks so much for the report!

Some initial thoughts. The .mjs extension signals a very strict handling of only ESM syntax and dependencies within modules, so at face value I'm not the most surprised this isn't working.

Before thinking about a PR, would you be able to shed some light on the requirements for needing both the .mjs and using ProvidePlugin? Or is the plugins injection something you only need in specific places etc.

My initial thoughts is that we definitely shouldn't throw if the two are being used independently. Before guiding you through a contribution, (which is super exciting nonetheless), I wanted to make sure this is Bug vs "Feature" (heavily quoted 😅)

This is expected since `ProvidePlugin` injects a `require` call and `javascript/esm` skips `require` interception. There are a few ways to solve this:

1. Disable `ProvidePlugin` for `javascript/esm`. https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/master/lib/ProvidePlugin.js#L79-L81
2. Or generate an `import` statement in `javascript/esm`

I think option 1 is the way to go.

I agree. 1 sounds the best to me as well.

@xandris how can I help you in submitting this PR?

To add some context here, I'm getting an identical error when trying to bundle a [module that references `process`](
https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/blob/5fe39262a308df944a87cc85b225228e7556aaa4/src/jsutils/instanceOf.js#L19) with close to no config on my part (i.e. no explicit use of `ProvidePlugin`). Would option 1 address the use case of referencing node builtins in `.mjs` files?

No this wouldn't address buildins. I would also disable these for now.

What's node.js plan for these global modules? Is `process` available or does it need to be imported via `import { process } from "node.js"`?

I can't seem to find any official comms from node.js on their plan for this, but can verify that with Node 9.11.1 and `--experimental-modules`, `process` is automatically available without importing anything.

Respectfully, would anyone care to elaborate on why option 2 isn't the preferred one? I mean, I know next to nothing about the Webpack codebase, but I see `import` injection as the closest thing to "correct" in this scenario. Especially with regards to keeping Node globals working, which otherwise is quite the breaking change for users of libraries that rely on them.

Actually option 2 is preferred, but it's really complex to do. The way these stuff is injected is pretty old (and I hope we could get rid of this soon). So option 1 will disable this feature for now, so it doesn't break anymore and we can figure out a way to improve the variable injection workflow.

repository.name: graphql-relay-js
repository.description: A library to help construct a graphql-js server supporting react-relay.

issue.body:
While working on optimising the bundling of https://github.com/graphql/swapi-graphql — for _reasons_<sup>1</sup> — I discovered that it was `import`ing things from `graphql-relay-js`, but that the latter, unlike `graphql-js`, only had a CommonJS entry point published to npm.

It might be desirable to add an ES module build target to this package, modeled on what `graphql-js` is [already doing](https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/blob/54f631ff3238affdddb4dc736fc282b620d70b15/package.json#L37).

---

<sup>1</sup> See https://twitter.com/motiz88/status/985110696668131328 - I'm investigating the [claim](https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-link/blob/a2025ad5a2eb7a1164d61a402e5deb227e14a84f/packages/apollo-link-schema/README.md) that schema execution on the front-end is impractical due to `graphql-js`'s [footprint](https://bundlephobia.com/result?p=graphql) in terms of bundle size. `swapi-graphql` simply happens to be a good, accessible testbed for just that (thanks @IvanGoncharov for the tip! 🙏)

issue.body:
Closes #208, with the actual build changes lifted nearly verbatim from `graphql-js` (e.g. https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/pull/1244)

* Sets `sideEffects: false` _a la_ the recently-merged https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/pull/1312.
* Works around an instance of https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/7032 (use of global `Buffer`) that would otherwise be encountered by users trying to actually bundle this as ESM with Webpack (e.g. what I'm currently doing with [`swapi-graphql`](https://github.com/graphql/swapi-graphql/compare/master...motiz88:webpack) as a testbed).
This is somewhat related to the issue with `process` fixed in https://github.com/graphql/graphql-js/commit/60c03ab23852074896fd9134c24c46ba595bf014 - except here, getting Node, Webpack and Flow to agree took some non-obvious fine-tuning, so I broke the solution out into its own heavily-commented file (`utils/buffer.js`). The Flow part can be simplified once ~https://github.com/facebook/flow/pull/6179~ hopefully lands.

UPDATE: https://github.com/facebook/flow/pull/6179 has landed and this branch incorporates the Flow 0.73 upgrade (which is also its own PR for good measure: https://github.com/graphql/graphql-relay-js/pull/210)

issue.title: Add Buffer property to buffer module

repository.name: flow
repository.description: Adds static typing to JavaScript to improve developer productivity and code quality.

issue.body:
Previously discussed or implemented in #5153, #3495, #2938, #3723, #3724 and maybe elsewhere.

This PR refines previous efforts by adding:

1. A correct, unambiguous type for `require("buffer").Buffer`:
```jsx
declare var Buffer: typeof global.Buffer;
```

2. A test.

To be clear: Per the Node [docs](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html), explicitly importing `Buffer` is rarely needed, given its availability in the global scope, but correct. It happens to be a viable option in environments where "magic" support for Node globals is either undesirable or broken (the latter is [currently](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/7032) the case for ES modules in Webpack).
